skill_traces.query:
Tim: Hey John! Long time no see! Been super busy lately. Guess what? Just skyped with that Harry Potter fan I met in CA and had a great time. We talked characters and maybe collab-ing - so cool to talk to someone who gets it. You? Anything new going on?
John: Hi Tim! Nice to hear from you. Glad you could reconnect. As for me, lots of stuff happened since we last talked. Last week I had a crazy game - crazy intense! We won it by a tight score. Scoring that last basket and hearing the crowd cheer was awesome!
Tim: Nice work! Bet it felt awesome to score that basket and have the crowd going wild. Must have been such an adrenaline rush! Did you manage to capture any other photos from the game?
John: Thanks! It was an amazing rush and just the one I showed you. We were so hyped!
Tim: Awesome! Winning a tough game must have been such an exhilarating experience!
John: Our team bond is awesome and it makes all the hard work worth it.
Tim: It's incredible how a team creates such strong ties. Having support like that is so important.
John: Thanks! You nailed it! Having a strong team/support is key - it's like a family away from home. We push each other to improve, and I'm so thankful for them.
Tim: That's great! Having a supportive team who are like family is awesome. Having people who motivate you and stick by you is priceless.
John: Definitely! They encourage me when I'm down too. It's not just in my sport, but in other aspects of life too. We hang out a lot and it's great having that bond.
Tim: Yeah, having another family is great. It definitely helps with my home life and hobbies.
John: Having someone to support and motivate you is so important, whether it's in sports or any other aspect of life. I know you've found your peace in reading fantasy books - that's amazing! What book are you currently reading? Anything that has stood out to you?
Tim: Thanks for asking! I'm reading a fantasy book that really captivates me. It takes me to another world where I'm on the edge of my seat and my imagination soars. It's amazing how books can transport us like that.
John: Books can be so captivating, taking us on such incredible journeys! What's the name of it?
Tim: It's a book by Patrick Rothfuss and it's awesome! The way the author builds the world and characters is amazing. You should read it!
John: Sounds cool! I'll definitely check it out. Thanks for the recommendation!
Tim: No problem! Let me know what you think after you read it.
John: Yep, I'll let you know once I'm done reading it. Thanks!
Tim: I hope you like it. Chat soon!
John: Me too. Talk to you soon!

selected.name: Extract Explicit Relational Framing
selected.description: When a user explicitly states how they view a person, pet, or group (e.g., 'pets are family', 'feel like family'), during extraction.
content: During extraction, if a user explicitly declares how they view someone or something (e.g., 'pets are family', 'my little family', 'feel like family', 'as a friend'), create a separate profile or relationship memory capturing that view, even if the message also contains event details like photos or activities.
Use memory kind 'relationship' when the statement defines a connection between the speaker and the subject; otherwise use 'state' or 'preference' for attitudes and values.
Apply to both first mentions and repeated mentions across sessions; record the view as a durable memory rather than folding it into an event memory.
Only extract when the framing is explicit or strongly implied; do not infer relationships from generic pleasantries, compliments, or small talk.
Stop after capturing the explicit view in one memory per stated relationship; do not add redundant memories for every photo or activity that merely implies the same view.
selected.rerank_reason: The conversation includes explicit relational framing such as 'like family' and 'supportive team,' which directly qualify how individuals view each other, meeting the criteria for this skill.

selected.name: Extract Shared Bonding-Activity Memories
selected.description: When a user reflectively describes a past shared activity with a specific person and frames it as bonding, making memories, or quality time.
content: During extraction, treat first-person statements about a past shared activity with a named person that explicitly mention bonding, making memories, closeness, or quality time as a durable event or relationship memory candidate.
Capture the activity, the companion, and the relational framing.
Do not require explicit fact-like phrasing; reflective storytelling is sufficient evidence.
Create at most one candidate per distinct activity-and-companion pair, and skip statements that name no specific person or activity.
selected.rerank_reason: The conversation reflects on shared activities with a specific person (team) and frames them as bonding experiences, making this skill applicable.

nearby_not_selected.name: Past Completed Activities as Events
nearby_not_selected.description: Use during extraction when a message includes a relative past-time phrase (e.g., 'two weeks ago', 'last month') describing an activity like reading, watching, or visiting.
content: When a user states they did something in the past with a relative time phrase (e.g., 'two weeks ago', 'last month', 'in January'), resolve the time from the message/session timestamp and record it as a completed event memory (e.g., 'read X in January 2023'), never as a current state, preference, or 'currently reading/watching/using' memory.
Do not merge a past completed activity with an ongoing current activity into a single memory; keep separate memories with distinct time spans and completion status.
Stop after creating the past event memory; do not expand to other activities unless explicitly mentioned.

nearby_not_selected.name: Location Qualifiers for Named Destination Plans
nearby_not_selected.description: When extracting or updating a plan memory that mentions a specific named venue, landmark, or business, include its commonly known location(s) so future location questions can be answered.
content: During extraction, if a plan memory mentions a specific named venue, landmark, or business, add a concise qualifier naming its well-known location(s), e.g., US states or countries.
Use only common knowledge about that entity; do not research or speculate beyond obvious, widely known locations.
If one location is commonly known, record it; if several prominent locations exist, record all commonly known ones, then stop.
Apply the same qualifier when updating an existing plan memory that references the venue.

nearby_not_selected.name: Resolve relative time in memory content
nearby_not_selected.description: When extracting a memory from a message that contains a relative time expression (e.g., next month, next week, tomorrow), resolve it to the absolute date using the message/session timestamp and include that absolute date in the content.
content: Applies during extraction: when a source message uses a relative time expression (next week, next month, tomorrow, in N days, etc.), resolve it to an absolute date using the message/session timestamp.
Write the resolved absolute date into the memory content itself (e.g., 'September 2023' instead of 'next month'); do not leave the relative phrase in the stored content.
Set world_start (and world_end if applicable) to the same resolved date so content and metadata are consistent.
Stop after resolving the expression; do not add extra details or searches.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Explicit Advice and Suggestions
nearby_not_selected.description: When a message contains explicit advice, suggestions, or recommendations from one participant to another, extract them as memory candidates.
content: During extraction, treat explicit advice, suggestions, and recommendations as memory-worthy. Capture the advisor, the recipient, the advised action, and the source message.
Preserve all distinct pieces of advice and their qualifiers; do not collapse or omit details. Tentative phrasing still counts.
Represent as an event or relationship memory; create at most one candidate per distinct piece of advice.
Stop after capturing the stated advice; do not infer outcomes or expand into related topics.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract implied vacation location memories
nearby_not_selected.description: When a user mentions a past vacation or trip with a location and a relative time (e.g., last summer, last year), extract an event memory for that time and place, resolving relative time from the message timestamp.
content: During extraction, if a message mentions a trip or vacation with a location and a relative time (e.g., last summer, last year), create an event memory for that trip. Resolve the relative time from the message timestamp; use the country as the location if only a city is named.
Do not skip such statements just because the trip is mentioned as background (e.g., describing a photo). If the location and time are clear, extract the event.
